SELECTED_INDEX: 5  
CONFIDENCE: 0.20  
EXPLANATION: The spectrum is dominated by strong aliphatic C–H stretches at 2878, 2912 and 2963 cm⁻¹ and by the familiar alkyl deformation bands at 1454, 1356 and their overtone at 2719 cm⁻¹ – all characteristic of a saturated hydrocarbon framework.  
A very intense line at 751 cm⁻¹ together with characteristic bands at 898, 956, 940 and 829 cm⁻¹ point to a five-membered cyclic ether (tetrahydrofuran‐type) skeleton, where C–O–C ring-breathing / ring-deformation and C–O stretching modes fall in the 700–950 cm⁻¹ region (Nakamoto GFQ-022 analogue). The presence of an additional C–O (or C–OH) stretch near 1171 cm⁻¹ supports an –OH substituent on the ring. Among the candidates, only OCC1CCCO1 (candidate 5: 2-hydroxytetrahydrofuran) contains a THF ring plus an exocyclic –CH₂OH group, matching both the ether and alcohol signatures as well as the abundant CH₂ groups indicated by the 2720 cm⁻¹ CH₂ overtone. No bands diagnostic for C=S (~1050–1200 cm⁻¹), N=N (~2100 cm⁻¹) or tertiary amine C–N stretches (~1010 cm⁻¹) are observed, disfavoring candidates 6, 8 and 9. Therefore candidate 5 gives the most coherent match to the observed Raman pattern.
